correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and edge cases are explicit. Sylvester symmetry gives |Q|=c/2; minimum generator yields ν=ceil(c/a). If a<a′ and equal c, c≥a′(a′−1)≥aa′ forces c/a−c/a′≥1 and hence distinct ceilings. The larger generator then follows from c=(a−1)(b−1). For a≥3 the two indecomposables are exactly a and b; they have distinct nilpotency exponents unless b=a+1, when the quotient is a truncated free commutative semigroup admitting precisely the swap. a=2 is monogenic or singleton. Independent code checks 919 pairs and 114 explicit swaps; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: This resolves the two-generated case of a stated conjecture concerning finite representations of numerical semigroups. More precisely, it identifies a pair of intrinsic and easily measurable semigroup invariants that completely reconstruct a natural infinite class and classifies the only nontrivial automorphism exceptions. This is structural reconstruction and not an arbitrary finite slice, despite its short elementary proof.
